title: The MCP phase trace names a busy-timeout wait in BEGIN IMMEDIATE, not only in the handler total
outcome: The MCP phase trace names a busy-timeout wait in BEGIN IMMEDIATE, not only in the handler total
acceptance: A BEGIN IMMEDIATE that gets the lock is still counted once, as today's contention test shows
A traced write refused after the store's busy timeout reports the wait in begin_immediate (count and max at least the timeout), shown by a Rust test that holds the write lock past the timeout
disposal_reason: Not a defect: SQLite profiles statements that end in SQLITE_BUSY. The observed gap came from a test that opened its traced store outside a traced call; the corrected test shows the timed-out wait in begin_immediate (5.5 s).
